entities.summary: Luis Fernando Castillo Mendez was a Venezuelan Independent Catholic priest who rose to the leadership of the Brazilian Catholic Apostolic Church (ICAB). Castillo Mendez was arguably the second or third patriarch of ICAB and its 48 dioceses, although none of his predecessors used that title. He was apparently the nominal head of a network of Iglesias Catolicas Apostolicas Nacionales (ICAN) or National Catholic Apostolic Churches and the Worldwide Communion of Catholic Apostolic National Churches (WCCAC), which were unsuccessful attempts to form an international association of Independent Catholic churches.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Luis Fernando Castillo Mendez's leadership of ICAB and its affiliated churches had a regional impact in South America during the 20th century, but his efforts to form an international association ultimately failed.
